hints: Focus on what replaces the Br in each reaction, OH, NH3 and CN all act as nucleophiles here.
Statements 1 and 2 work cleanly, Br is swapped for OH to give ethanol and for NH2 to give ethylamine.
Count carbons carefully for the cyanide reaction, adding CN always adds one extra carbon to the chain.
walkthrough:
**Recall nucleophilic substitution of bromoethane**

Great start, Br is a good leaving group. A nucleophile attacks the carbon and Br leaves as $\text{Br}^-$.

General pattern:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{Nu}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Nu} + \text{Br}^-$$

**Check statements 1 and 2**

With aqueous NaOH, $\text{OH}^-$ replaces Br to give ethanol. That is correct.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{Br}^-$$
With ethanolic $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{NH}_3$ replaces Br to give ethylamine, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$. That is also correct.

**Spot the trap in statement 3**

With KCN, $\text{CN}^-$ replaces Br, but the CN carbon becomes part of the main product. So you gain a carbon.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{CN}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN} + \text{Br}^-$$
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CN}$ has 3 carbons, so it is propanenitrile, not ethanenitrile. Statement 3 is false, so only 1 and 2 are correct.

options.A: Incorrect, this claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 1 and 2 are right, but 3 names the wrong nitrile, so this overcounts.
options.B: Correct, only 1 and 2 are true. Aqueous NaOH gives ethanol and ethanolic NH3 gives ethylamine, while statement 3 is false because the product is propanenitrile, not ethanenitrile.
options.C: Incorrect, this includes statement 3 and misses statement 1. Statement 3 is false due to the extra carbon from cyanide, and statement 1 is definitely true.
options.D: Incorrect, this claims only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is also correct because ammonia acts as a nucleophile to form the primary amine, ethylamine.
